question: Should OpenClaw officially expose the first-party Android app as a system Sharesheet target for text, links, and bounded image imports?
rationale: The implementation fits existing architecture, but it adds a new exported, platform-visible capability and accepted-content policy that requires Android product ownership.

options.title: Sponsor bounded sharing
options.body: Accept editable text, link, and image drafts with strict URI and count limits plus real-device proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to text first
options.body: Approve text and link imports now while deferring image and multi-share handling.

options.title: Decline the target
options.body: Keep cross-app import manual and avoid expanding the Android app's exported intent surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor bounded sharing
recommendation.body: Accept editable text, link, and image drafts with strict URI and count limits plus real-device proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the current intent-routing, typed-draft, and attachment seams that the feature extends.
